title: Interspecies communication
gist: MIT Technology Review scores interspecies communication 4/10: AI now detects and attributes animal calls, but real translation remains theoretical and a two-way conversation is of uncertain feasibility. Earth Species Project's NatureLM is a leading bet, with skeptics warning of acoustic-similarity errors.

insights.claim: Decoding requires matching sounds to context, as with prairie dogs giving different yips for a coyote than for a hawk, which is slow for hard-to-observe species such as deep-diving whales or subterranean mole rats.
insights.speaker: Cassandra Willyard
insights.so_what: Data collection, not compute, is the bottleneck for most species.

insights.claim: Many animals communicate via visual cues, touch or pheromones, some hard for humans to perceive, and with no multispecies Rosetta stone there is no ground truth to check translation accuracy.
insights.speaker: Cassandra Willyard
insights.so_what: Audio-only models will capture only part of the signal, and validation is structurally hard.

insights.claim: Over the last decade AI has enabled detection of calls, attribution of sounds to individual animals and pattern spotting, building on hydrophones and wearable biologgers.
insights.speaker: Cassandra Willyard
insights.so_what: Pattern-detection tools are real and sellable today; translation is not.

insights.claim: The Earth Species Project (nonprofit founded 2018) used machine learning to detect carrion crow vocalizations and identify which bird made which call.
insights.speaker: Cassandra Willyard
insights.so_what: Concrete but modest proof point: identification, not meaning.
insights.locator: Researchers at the Earth Species Project

insights.claim: ESP hopes NatureLM, trained on human speech, music and animal sounds, will interpret vocalizations across species, on the logic that LLMs excel at finding relationships between words; this remains theoretical.
insights.speaker: Cassandra Willyard
insights.so_what: Cross-modal transfer from human language to animals is an unproven assumption.
insights.quote: That promise, however, is still theoretical.

insights.claim: Neuroecologist Yossi Yovel warns models may overweight acoustic similarity and lump together similar sounds that have different meanings.
insights.speaker: Cassandra Willyard
insights.so_what: A plausible failure mode that could yield confident but wrong translations.

insights.claim: Con Slobodchikoff of Zoolingua, which works on dog-to-human speech, argues many animals share enough evolutionary structure that understanding them should be possible, while it is unclear when or whether two-way conversation will happen.
insights.speaker: Cassandra Willyard
insights.so_what: Commercial pet-translation products are ahead of the science.

insights.claim: MIT Technology Review rates interspecies communication 4 out of 10: lots of data amassed, but no way yet to decipher it.
insights.speaker: Cassandra Willyard
insights.so_what: Lowest-scoring of the pieces in this batch, reflecting early-stage science.
insights.quote: Researchers have amassed heaps of data on animal communication
